back: A profit-seeking bank that accepts deposits, makes loans and provides payment services to households and firms.

front: Three main functions of commercial banks?
back: Accept deposits; make loans and overdrafts; provide payment services (transfers, cards, cheques). Also foreign exchange, safe custody, advice.
The bank that issues the currency, is banker to the government and to banks, acts as lender of last resort, runs monetary policy and supervises banks (Zimbabwe: the RBZ).

front: What is a **lender of last resort**?
back: The central bank lending to banks short of cash when no one else will, to stop a bank failing and a panic spreading.
Initial deposit ÷ reserve ratio (as a decimal). Credit multiplier = 1 ÷ reserve ratio.
Loans are profitable but illiquid; cash is liquid but earns nothing. Banks must hold enough cash to meet withdrawals.
Serve firms: arrange finance, underwrite share issues, advise on mergers, accept bills of exchange.
Take savings from the public and lend mainly for house purchase (mortgages).

front: Why can't a sound bank repay all deposits at once?
back: Most deposits have been lent out; only a fraction is held as cash reserves.
